jobs.description:
Manage a Team of Ops Associates for a fast-growing NYC-based custom apparel start-up (Remote)

Hi, this is Arpana, one of the founding members of Fresh Prints.

In December 2016, I came across a job post on Naukri from Jacob Goodman, one of the co-owners of Fresh Prints. They were looking for someone to lead Operations in India. The post had already been taken down, but I decided to send Jacob an email anyway. To my surprise, he replied, and soon I found myself stepping into what would become a life-changing opportunity.

During the interview process, it became clear just how new everything was. There was no office, no payroll system, no established infrastructure. But what stood out was Jacob and Josh's unwavering belief in the vision they had for Fresh Prints. They didn't have all the answers, but their passion was contagious, and I knew I wanted to help build something from the ground up.

So I jumped in. I found an office, figured out payroll, and even brought in my childhood best friend to help get things started. Those early days were full of unknowns, but that's what made them so exciting. I got to wear multiple hats, solve problems on the fly, and help build something tangible. What started as a team of two soon grew into teams across Finance, Tech, and Marketing.

As the first employee of Fresh Prints India, I've had the privilege of helping shape the company from its earliest days. After taking a short break to have my daughter, I returned to lead HR and Recruiting. Since then, we've grown from a scrappy startup into a team of 400+ people across three countries. But even today, we still believe it's day one.

One of the moments I'm most proud of was how we navigated COVID-19 together. Overnight, universities shut down, events stopped, and we went from million-dollar months to zero revenue.

But we'd spent years preparing for uncertainty. From day one, we believed our balance sheet had to be a strength, so we always planned to be able to operate for at least a year without revenue or layoffs. When COVID hit, we were scared, but we were prepared.

Then we adapted. As demand for PPE surged, we pivoted from custom apparel to supplying protective equipment. It wasn't just about keeping the business alive—it was about meeting a real need. That willingness to move quickly and solve problems together helped us come out stronger while many companies were simply trying to survive.

The opportunities that were available to me when I joined as the first employee are still here today—in fact, they're even bigger. We're at an exciting point in our journey, and we're looking for people who want to have a real impact on what comes next.

If you're someone who sees opportunity and isn't afraid to chase it, this is the role for you. We're looking for people with an entrepreneurial mindset who take ownership, challenge the norm, and enjoy solving problems without a playbook. At Fresh Prints, there are no limits—but if you're looking for a role with a clear set of instructions, this probably isn't it.

If our story resonates, we want to hear from you!

Here's more about the Operations Manager role:

The operations team handles the most crucial part of the business and is directly responsible for every step in delivering the end product to our customers.

  • How do we build a team that drives the business forward?
  • How do we motivate Operations Associates to respond to a higher volume of tickets at an even higher quality?
  • How do you most efficiently manage incoming requests from printers, customers, and Campus Managers?

jobs.description:
This is a once-in-a-generation leadership role for an executive who has lived through the defining technology transformations of the last two decades—ERP, cloud, digital, and data—and is now positioned to define what comes next: the Agentic enterprise.

As Senior Vice President of Agentic Transformation, you will be Blend360's most senior client-facing executive for this practice. You will own the non-technical consulting relationship across our Fortune 1000 and Private Equity client portfolio—leading the strategic framing, organizational readiness, executive alignment, and change management dimensions of complex, multi-year agentic transformation engagements.

You will not be writing code or architecting technical systems. You will be the executive who walks into a boardroom with a newly appointed CAIO or a skeptical CFO and earns the credibility and trust to shepherd their organization through a fundamental shift in how work gets done. You will translate Blend360's technical capabilities into business imperatives—and you will build the client relationships that define our firm's reputation in this market.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Client Leadership & Executive Engagement

  • Own senior-most consulting relationships with C-Suite executives (CEO, CFO, COO, CAIO, CTO) at Fortune 1000 and PE-portfolio clients across transformation engagements.

  • Serve as Blend360's trusted strategic advisor to client leadership—guiding them through the business case, organizational implications, and risk landscape of agentic adoption.

  • Lead executive steering committees, board-level briefings, and transformation governance forums on behalf of our clients.

  • Cultivate deep, multi-year relationships that expand Blend360's footprint within accounts and generate new opportunities through referral and reputation.

Transformation Strategy & Program Leadership

  • Lead the design and facilitation of Agentic Transformation roadmaps—defining the sequencing, business value, and organizational change required to move clients from current state to agentic maturity.

  • Frame transformation in terms of business outcomes: cost efficiency, revenue growth, competitive differentiation, risk reduction—not technology outputs.

  • Draw on deep institutional knowledge of prior technology transformation waves (ERP, cloud migration, digital, data/analytics) to contextualize what is different and what is the same about the agentic era.

  • Partner with Blend360's technical and delivery teams to ensure the business and organizational elements of transformation are integrated seamlessly into the overall program design and execution.

Organizational Readiness & Change Management

  • Assess and guide organizational readiness for agentic transformation—spanning culture, workforce, governance, operating model, and change capacity.

  • Help clients design the structures, roles, and accountability models needed to sustain agentic operating models beyond initial implementation.

  • Drive stakeholder alignment and manage organizational resistance at senior levels, including navigating political dynamics within complex enterprises.

  • Translate technical complexity into clear, resonant narratives for non-technical executives and boards.

Practice & Market Development

  • Collaborate with Blend360's leadership team to evolve our Agentic Transformation service portfolio, methodologies, and go-to-market narrative.

  • Contribute to thought leadership—white papers, keynotes, executive roundtables—that positions Blend360 as the definitive partner for enterprise agentic transformation.

  • Support business development and proposal efforts, including executive-level presentations and solution framing for new client opportunities.

  • Mentor and develop consulting talent, codifying your hard-won transformation expertise into Blend360's institutional playbooks and frameworks.

Experience & Background

  • Partner Level Experience with top tier management consulting firm (McKinsey, Bain, BCG, Alix Partners, PWC etc.)

  • 20+ years of progressive consulting or senior advisory experience, with a significant portion spent leading large-scale technology transformation engagements at Fortune 1000 or equivalent organizations.

  • Proven track record of owning and growing C-Suite relationships in an advisory or consulting capacity—not just participating in them.

  • Deep, hands-on experience with at least two or more of the major enterprise transformation waves: ERP (SAP, Oracle), cloud migration, digital transformation, data/analytics modernization, or platform consolidation.

  • Demonstrable experience in Private Equity environments—either as an advisor to PE-portfolio companies during transformation programs or in an operating role within a PE-backed business.

  • Familiarity with the emerging agentic AI landscape—including enterprise AI agents, autonomous process orchestration, and the organizational implications of human-agent collaboration—sufficient to engage credibly with technically sophisticated clients and internal teams.

Leadership & Consulting Competencies

  • Commanding gravitas and credibility with CEOs, board members, and investor groups—particularly in ambiguous, high-stakes environments. Executive presence

  • The ability to translate technical complexity and organizational ambiguity into clear, compelling strategic narratives that drive executive alignment and decision-making. Strategic framing

  • A track record of building multi-year, trust-based relationships with senior clients that transcend individual engagements. Relationship depth

  • Experience guiding organizations through significant resistance, uncertainty, and disruption—with the empathy and tenacity to see transformations through. Change leadership

  • The ability to anchor all recommendations in financial impact and business value—not technology for its own sake. Business acumen

  • Comfort working in a matrix consulting environment, partnering with technical leads, delivery managers, and subject matter experts to drive integrated client outcomes. Collaborative execution

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

YEAR ONE

Trusted by 3–5 flagship clients; embedded in active transformation programs; Blend360's SVP voice at the C-Suite table.

YEAR TWO

Established as a market-recognized thought leader in agentic transformation; $15–25M in managed/influenced revenue; scaled playbooks adopted firm-wide.

ONGOING

Blend360 is the named partner of choice for agentic transformation among Fortune 1000 and PE clients; SVP is the reason clients renew, expand, and refer.

TEAM LEGACY

A generation of Blend360 consultants shaped by your frameworks, mentorship, and institutional knowledge of transformation excellence.

WHY BLEND360

This is not a role at a firm that is hoping to build an AI practice someday. Blend360 is already executing. At TE, you will unleash your potential working with people from diverse backgrounds and industries to create a safer, sustainable and more connected world.

Job Overview

The NPI (New Product Introduction) Supply Chain Manager serves as the critical link between product development and mass manufacturing, ensuring a seamless transition from concept to commercialization. This role leads the end-to-end supply chain workstream for new product introductions, driving cross-functional alignment, supports supplier readiness, Bill of Materials (BOM) integrity, and risk mitigation throughout the product development lifecycle. The ideal candidate combines strong project management skills with deep supply chain expertise to deliver successful product launches on schedule, within budget, and at target quality levels.

Job Responsibilities

New Product Introduction (NPI) Leadership
• Lead the supply chain workstream for new product introductions from concept development through commercialization and manufacturing handoff.
• Develop and manage NPI supply chain project plans, milestones, deliverables, and launch readiness activities.
• Collaborate closely with Engineering, Product Management, Operations, Quality, Manufacturing, and Procurement teams to ensure launch success.
BOM and Material Readiness Management
• Own BOM health throughout the product development lifecycle, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and alignment with sourcing strategies.
• Drive timely component selection, qualification, and release activities.
• Monitor engineering changes and assess impacts to supply chain readiness, cost, inventory, and manufacturing execution.
Supplier Readiness and Development
• Support the evaluation of supplier capabilities, capacity, and readiness by partnering with Procurement, Supplier Quality, Engineering, and Operations teams to identify launch-related risks and gaps.
• Assist with supplier onboarding, qualification, tooling, sample builds, and production ramp activities by helping coordinate inputs, timing, and cross-functional follow-up.
• Monitor supplier readiness milestones and support tracking of key metrics, helping ensure visibility to supplier progress, risks, and launch commitments for quality, cost, and delivery.
Risk Management and Mitigation
• Identify, assess, and proactively mitigate supply chain risks related to materials, suppliers, logistics, capacity, and product transitions.
• Develop contingency plans and alternate sourcing strategies to minimize launch disruptions.
• Lead risk reviews and provide clear escalation paths for critical issues.
S&OP Linkage and Forecast Alignment
• Ensure clear linkage between NPI activities and the S&OP process, including visibility to demand forecast assumptions, launch timing, ramp volumes, and corresponding supply response plans.
• Partner with Commercial, Product Management, Supply Planning, Manufacturing, and Operations teams to ensure assumptions driving the forecast are clearly communicated, understood, and documented.
• Align demand expectations with manufacturing site readiness, capacity plans, material availability, and supplier constraints; where demand and supply assumptions differ, ensure gaps, risks, and decision points are transparent.
• Escalate capacity constraints, supply risks, or site readiness concerns identified through communication with manufacturing sites and cross-functional planning teams.
• Maintain regular communication with manufacturing plants to confirm deliverables, timing, site readiness, and escalation needs to ensure launch activities remain on schedule.
Cross-Functional Project Management
• Facilitate communication and alignment across global stakeholders.
• Drive accountability through regular project reviews, status updates, and executive reporting.
• Manage dependencies, critical paths, and issue resolution to support product launch timelines.
• Proactively challenge assumptions, speak up when risks or issues are observed, and drive timely resolution to keep projects on track.
Commercialization and Manufacturing Handoff
• Ensure supply chain readiness for pilot builds, validation builds, and production ramp-up.
• Coordinate the transition from development to sustaining operations.
• Verify that processes, suppliers, inventory strategies, and operational controls are established for successful high-volume manufacturing.

Preferred

  • Experience in high-tech, consumer electronics, medical device, automotive, industrial, or advanced manufacturing environments.
  • Knowledge of product lifecycle management (PLM), cost management, and supplier quality processes.
  • Experience working with global suppliers and international manufacturing

Key Competencies

  • Supply Chain Strategy & Execution
  • S&OP Integration, Forecast Assumption Alignment, and Supply Response Planning
  • New Product Introduction (NPI) Management
  • Bill of Materials (BOM) Governance
  • Supplier Readiness & Development
  • Risk Assessment & Mitigation
  • Cross-Functional Leadership

Proactive Ownership, Constructive Challenge, and Issue Escalation

  • Program & Project Management
  • Manufacturing Ramp & Commercialization
  • Executive Communication & Stakeholder Management
  • Problem Solving & Data-Driven Decision Making

Success Measures

  • On-time product launch execution.

jobs.description:
Please submit your CV in English and indicate your level of English proficiency.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based, not permanent employment.

What this opportunity involves

We're building competitive-programming problems and their automatic graders (test cases + checkers) used to train advanced AI coding models. You'll create problems, write both correct and deliberately-wrong solutions, and design the tough test cases that catch subtly-broken code. Your work is what makes the training signal trustworthy.

To apply, share: your competitive-programming handle(s) + current/peak rating, any problem-setting experience, and IOI/ICPC/olympiad history.

What you'll do

  • Write original algorithmic problems — clear statement, sound constraints, an intended solution;
  • Write correct solutions in C++ and Python;
  • Write realistic wrong solutions (common mistakes) to test against;
  • Build and harden test cases: generators, edge cases, stress and "hacking" tests;
  • Write checkers/interactors (testlib) for problems with more than one valid answer;
  • Confirm the quality bar: correct solutions pass, wrong ones fail, within time limits.

What we look for

  • Strong competitive programming background, shown by a public profile — a Codeforces rating (see levels below), OR an IOI / ICPC / national-olympiad record;
  • Fluent contest C++ (STL, complexity); comfortable writing Python;
  • Can explain why a solution is wrong and build an input that breaks it;
  • Strong written English (C1+).

Levels (by Codeforces rating, or equivalent olympiad achievement):

  • Associate — 1700–2100 (Expert / Candidate Master): easier problems;
  • Expert — 2200–2600 (Master / Grandmaster): harder problems
  • Senior / Reviewer — 2600+ (Int'l Grandmaster) or IOI/ICPC medalist: hardest problems + quality review.

Nice to have

  • IOI / ICPC alumni and top competitive programmers especially encouraged to apply;
  • Experience setting or testing problems for real contests (Codeforces rounds, ICPC, national olympiads, online judges);
  • Testlib experience (checkers, validators, generators);
  • Experience creating data for LLM code benchmarks or similar RL / evaluation datasets.

How it works

Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join a project → Complete tasks → Get paid

Project time expectations

For this project, tasks are estimated to require around 10-20 hours per week during active phases, based on project requirements. This is an estimate, not a guaranteed workload, and applies only while the project is active. Tasks must be submitted by the deadline and meet the listed acceptance criteria to be accepted.

Compensation

Paid per accepted task. Your rate depends on the qualification tier you reach and how efficiently you complete tasks. Because payment is per task, a faster pace raises your effective hourly rate.

Join Revive Media to help advertisers across the country scale their localized Connected TV advertising. Our business is growing rapidly and we’re in the midst of transforming from a services agency to a product-led business with our new native platform. The platform is live with external partners and we're expanding its reach - this role will help drive broader adoption, improve the experience for existing users, and scale usage across new channels and customers.

We are a small, remote-first team of high-performing professionals with diverse backgrounds located across many time zones, including North America, Europe, and Asia. We prioritize asynchronous communication and documentation but come together as a team to solve hard problems.


Position Overview

As a Senior Product Manager, your focus will be on Revive's campaign planning experience — helping our users build the best possible campaign proposals that convert to sold-through, high-performing campaigns. This means driving the automation of the proposal workflow, enhancing our targeting recommendations, and building tools that expand our inventory offering — including cross-platform forecasting capabilities that give sellers and account teams confidence in what they're proposing.

You'll take full ownership of an active squad's roadmap and partner closely with Engineering, Design, Sales/Account Strategy, and Operations to ship improvements that reduce friction, improve proposal quality, and drive measurable business outcomes.

Responsibilities

  • Squad roadmap ownership: Own and drive an existing squad's roadmap — including quarterly planning, backlog prioritization, intake, and stakeholder alignment — stepping into a team that has active in-flight initiatives and an established ways of working
  • Cross-platform forecasting: Lead the development of a forecasting mechanisms that gives confidence in proposal deliverability and scale across programmatic and direct channels; iterate based on adoption signals and seller feedback
  • Pre-sales workflow improvements: Partner with cross-functional teams to improve the end-to-end proposal creation workflow (inputs, recommendations, packaging, outputs) to reduce cycle time and increase win rate
  • Quality & reliability: Reduce errors, edge cases, and operational friction that slow down proposal creation or harm trust — including category validation and eligibility rules as foundational elements of a reliable, automated proposal system
  • Product requirements: Translate user needs into clear PRDs, workflows, acceptance criteria, and rollout plans
  • Cross-functional delivery: Partner with engineering and design to deliver high-quality features on time
  • Enablement & adoption: Support rollout and training for sales/account teams; ensure tools are actually used in the proposal process
  • System knowledge: Build a strong understanding of upstream/downstream systems (data, targeting, inventory, reporting) that shape proposal quality


Success metrics

  • Improved proposal win rate and platform adoption, leading to more proposals sold through
  • Improved campaign outcomes driven by better upfront targeting and packaging
  • Reduced proposal turnaround time by automating qualified proposals

What to expect in your first 90 days

Month 1 — Get your bearings

    • Learn Revive's proposal workflow end-to-end and how targeting is sold and fulfilled
    • Get up to speed on in-flight squad initiatives and metrics
    • Shadow sales/account teams; review recent wins/losses and where proposals break down

Month 2 — Dive into the backlog

    • Prioritize the backlog (impact vs effort vs operational cost), with a focus on the proposal funnel
    • Ship 1–2 improvements that measurably reduce friction or improve proposal quality
    • Tighten requirements + feedback loops with sales/account teams and engineering/design

Month 3 — Product roadmap ownership

    • Align on a 3 to 6-month roadmap (presales improvements + targeting expansion)
    • Establish full ownership of the squad roadmap and operating rhythms
    • Kick off a larger initiative tied to conversion (e.g., audience packaging, packaging expansion, feasibility/scale validation)

Requirements

  • 7+ years of product management experience (B2B SaaS or platform products preferred)
  • Experience with ad tech fundamentals, particularly audience targeting, programmatic inventory constraints, and cross-platform delivery considerations
  • Demonstrated experience improving user-facing workflows or journeys, with a track record of shipping UX improvements (e.g. increased feature adoption, reduced drop-off, faster task completion)
  • Proven ability to translate user needs into clear requirements for complex systemStrong written and verbal communication skills (remote-first)
  • Demonstrated experience shipping AI-powered product features with measurable user impact (e.g., recommendations, automation, or intelligent workflows)

Benefits

  • We're fully Remote and offer a remote working stipend

jobs.excerpt: Willkommen bei Glow25! Bei Glow25 verbinden wir Beauty mit Wissenschaft und modernster Technologie – KI gehört bei uns ganz selbstverständlich zum Arbeitsalltag.
jobs.description:
Willkommen bei Glow25!

Bei Glow25 verbinden wir Beauty mit Wissenschaft und modernster Technologie – KI gehört bei uns ganz selbstverständlich zum Arbeitsalltag. Als Deutschlands führende Kollagen-Marke begleiten wir Menschen dabei, sich in jeder Lebensphase wohlzufühlen und ihre natürliche Schönheit zu unterstreichen.

Für unser weiteres Wachstum suchen wir Menschen mit Substanz: zuverlässig, motiviert und mit echtem Interesse daran, gemeinsam etwas Bedeutendes aufzubauen. Bei Glow25 triffst du auf ambitionierte Ziele und ein Umfeld, das Eigenverantwortung fördert und Leistung wertschätzt – unabhängig davon, welche Rolle du übernimmst.

Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.

Das sind unsere aktuellen Herausforderungen und perspektivischen Ziele:

Als Supply Chain Controller (all genders) baust du ein modernes Controlling für unsere Lieferkette auf und agierst als Business Partner für unser Operations Management Team. Du sorgst für Transparenz in einem Bereich, der für unser Wachstum entscheidend ist, und bringst deine Controlling-Expertise direkt in operative Entscheidungen ein.

In diesem Bereich brauchen wir Deine Unterstützung:

  • Du übernimmst die Verantwortung für die Vorratsbewertung und entwickelst das Inventory Controlling kontinuierlich weiter.

  • Du baust Transparenz über Bestände, Warenbewegungen und deren finanziellen Einfluss auf.

  • Du analysierst zentrale Supply-Chain- und Operations-KPIs wie Bestände, COGS, Logistikkosten und Forecast Accuracy.

  • Du agierst als Business Partner für Operations, Supply Chain und Procurement und bringst finanzielle Perspektiven in operative Entscheidungen ein.

  • Du unterstützt bei Budgetplanung, Forecasts und der operativen Finanzplanung.

  • Du baust Dashboards, Reportingstrukturen und KPIs auf und entwickelst sie weiter.

  • Du erstellst Business Cases für operative Entscheidungen, zum Beispiel zu Lieferanten, Logistikstrukturen oder Bestandsstrategien.

  • Du identifizierst Kosten- und Working-Capital-Optimierungspotenziale entlang der gesamten Wertschöpfungskette.

Du bringst folgende Erfahrungen mit:

  • Du hast ein Studium der Betriebswirtschaft, Finance, Supply Chain Management, Wirtschaftswissenschaften oder eines vergleichbaren Fachbereichs abgeschlossen.

  • Du bringst mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im Controlling, Operations Finance, Supply Chain Analytics oder Consulting mit.

  • Du hast einschlägige Erfahrungen mit Beständen, Kostenstrukturen oder operativen KPIs.

  • Du denkst analytisch, arbeitest datengetrieben und kannst komplexe Zusammenhänge klar und verständlich aufbereiten.

  • Du arbeitest strukturiert und eigenständig und behältst auch in einem dynamischen Umfeld den Überblick.

  • Du hast sehr gute Kenntnisse in Excel oder Google Sheets und bewegst dich sicher in der Welt der Zahlen.

  • Du hast Erfahrung mit BI-Tools wie Power BI oder Tableau oder bist motiviert, dich schnell einzuarbeiten.

  • Du hast idealerweise bereits mit ERP-Systemen oder Finanzsystemen gearbeitet.

  • Du interessierst dich für Datenanalyse, Reporting und die Entwicklung aussagekräftiger KPIs.

Das sind Charakterzüge, die Dich beschreiben:

• Du bist analytisch stark und liebst es, komplexe Zusammenhänge zu durchdringen.
• Du bist ein Teamplayer mit ausgeprägter Kommunikationsstärke.
• Du arbeitest strukturiert, eigenverantwortlich und lösungsorientiert.
• Du bist proaktiv und bringst Themen selbstständig voran.
• Du bist flexibel und behältst auch in dynamischen Situationen den Überblick.

Diese Rolle passt eher nicht zu dir, wenn...

  • ...du am liebsten für dich allein arbeitest und wenig Austausch mit anderen Teams suchst. Die Rolle lebt vom laufenden Business Partnering mit Production, Supply Chain und Procurement.

  • ...dir der Einstieg ins Controlling noch fehlt. Wir suchen jemanden mit bereits gefestigter Praxiserfahrung, nicht für eine Einstiegsposition.

  • ...du dich ungern mit Tabellen, Kennzahlen und Datenanalyse beschäftigst. Excel/Google Sheets sind hier tägliches Handwerkszeug.

  • ...du feste Prozesse ohne Weiterentwicklung bevorzugst.

Darauf kannst du dich freuen:

  • Arbeite flexibel, so wie es am besten zu dir passt. Arbeite dann und dort, wo du am produktivsten bist – mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten und smarter Zeiterfassung.

  • Glow Card – jeden Monat ein Bonus. 50 € Guthaben monatlich für lokale Anbieter – macht 600 € im Jahr extra für dich.

  • Weiterkommen leicht gemacht. Mit unserer Glowcademy und Lernzeit pro Woche bleibst du immer am Ball.

  • 40 % Mitarbeiterrabatt. Auf das komplette Sortiment – das lohnt sich wirklich.

  • Urlaub, der dir guttut. 30 Tage frei + 1 persönlicher Feiertag + bis zu 10 unbezahlte Tage extra, wenn du mal länger abschalten willst.

  • Gesundheit im Fokus. Wir übernehmen bis zu 600 € im Jahr für Zusatzleistungen – von Brille bis Zahnreinigung.

  • Für später gut abgesichert. Nach der Probezeit gibt’s 600 € Zuschuss zur Altersvorsorge – und wenn du selbst mit einzahlst, legen wir nochmal 20 % drauf.

  • Corporate Benefits & FutureBens. Hol dir exklusive Rabatte und Vorteile bei vielen Partnern.

  • Kultur, die wirklich strahlt. Seit fünf Jahren in Folge sind wir als Top Company bei Kununu ausgezeichnet - ein echtes Zeichen für unsere starke, positive und gelebte Kultur.

  • Move your way. Vom Workout bis zur Wellness-Auszeit - du entscheidest, wie du dich fit hältst. Mit Urban Sports Club oder Wellpass hast du die Wahl.

Yay! Du hast es bis hierher geschafft!

Wenn du jetzt immer noch liest, ist die Wahrscheinlichkeit groß, dass wir ein Match sind.

Eine Sache liegt uns aber noch am Herzen: Trau dich! Vor allem als Frau oder als jemand einer unterrepräsentierten Bevölkerungsgruppe. Auch wenn du nicht überall einen Haken setzen kannst, möchten wir dich ermutigen, dich trotzdem zu bewerben. Wir glauben, dass eine bunte Vielfalt von Perspektiven und Erfahrungen ein Team stärker macht – und je stärker unser Team ist, desto besser erreichen wir unsere Mission, Menschen zu mehr Energie im Alltag zu verhelfen.

If you’re detail-oriented, comfortable working across multiple systems, and naturally notice when something doesn’t add up, this could be a strong fit.

Administrative & Leadership Support

    • Documentation

jobs.excerpt: At Sysdig, we believe cloud security isn't a compromise - it's a promise.
jobs.description:
At Sysdig, we believe cloud security isn't a compromise - it's a promise. From the start, our mission has been clear: to help organizations secure innovation in the cloud, the right way.
We created Falco, the open standard for cloud threat detection, and continue to lead the cloud security market with runtime insights, open innovation, and agentic Al. Creators of technology trusted by over 60% of the Fortune 500, Sysdig gives teams the real-time clarity to move fast and defend what matters most.
Culture matters here. We believe diversity fuels stronger ideas, and open dialogue drives sharper decisions. Recognized as a Best Place to Work and one of Deloitte's fastest-growing companies for the past 5 years, we're here to raise the standard for what cloud security and workplace culture should be.
If you have the passion to dig deeper, the desire to challenge convention, and the curiosity to build something better, Sysdig is the right place for you.

What you will do

  • Own the vision, strategy, and execution of field marketing across AMER, EMEA, and APJ — building a scalable center of excellence (plans, playbooks, reporting) that keeps every region consistent while localizing where it matters, and acts as the voice of the field back to global GTM.
  • Own the end-to-end ABM and territory demand gen strategy across events, digital, content, and outbound — driven by intent and account-fit data, engineered for asymmetric security buying committees, and inclusive of named accountability for Sysdig's visibility in AI-assisted discovery (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, AI Overviews).
  • Set the strategy, standards, and calendar for the full event portfolio (RSAC, Black Hat, KubeCon, hosted summits, CISO dinners, partner events) — rebalancing deliberately toward owned, intimate, experience-led formats with rigorous ROI discipline and executive engagement that gets Sysdig leaders in front of buying committees earlier.
  • Serve as the senior marketing partner to regional sales and RevOps — aligning on territory strategy, whitespace, pipeline, and revenue through territory planning, forecasts, and QBRs, while developing strategic co-marketing with cloud, technology, and channel partners to scale through-partner pipeline.
  • Own and forecast the global field marketing budget and establish a data-centric operating model — clear KPIs, multi-method measurement (attribution, incrementality, win-loss), and clean bidirectional integration across the event stack, Marketo, and Salesforce — holding every program accountable for ROI and pipeline contribution.
  • Build, lead, and develop a high-performing distributed team and operationalize a "human + AI" model — turning higher-value AI use cases (event selection, agentic list building, personalized follow-up at scale) into repeatable, measured workflows with clear quality guardrails, while communicating strategy and performance to executive stakeholders.

What you will bring with you

  • 10+ years of B2B marketing experience, including 5+ years leading and building field, regional, or demand generation teams — ideally distributed across multiple geographies.
  • Deep familiarity with the enterprise cybersecurity or cloud infrastructure buyer. You understand how CISOs, security architects, and platform teams actually evaluate, and how procurement, legal, and finance shape the outcome.
  • Proven track record owning a multi-million-dollar budget and a pipeline number, with the receipts to show measurable revenue impact at scale.
  • Expertise across the full demand funnel, ABM, intent data, and enterprise event execution — with a strong point of view on where field investment does and does not pay back.
  • Demonstrated AI fluency as a builder, not just a user. You have put AI into real marketing workflows and can point to what you built, what it replaced, and what it produced. You have a clear view on where AI genuinely creates leverage versus where it is hype.
  • Hands-on command of a modern GTM stack: Marketo, Salesforce, an ABM/intent platform (6sense, Demandbase, or similar), event tech, and BI/reporting. Comfort with AI-native GTM tooling is a strong plus.
  • Track record of operating as a strategic leader — building cross-functional partnerships, influencing executive stakeholders, making the business case, and leading planning across regions and time zones.
  • Willingness to travel meaningfully, roughly 20-40%, including some evenings and weekends around major industry moments.

What we look for

  • A strategic, business-minded leader who balances big-picture vision with hands-on execution. At this level, the job is to build the system that runs the programs.
  • A pipeline mindset. You measure success in opportunities and revenue influenced, not attendance or lead counts. You know the number a program will produce before it happens and you prove the one it did after.
  • Strong people leadership. You hire well, develop people, and get the best out of a team spread across three regions.
  • Executive presence and the ability to influence and align stakeholders without direct authority.
  • Intellectual honesty about what is working. You kill your own programs when the data says to.
  • Genuine curiosity about how this discipline is changing, and the confidence to rebuild rather than defend. A “we have always done it this way” mindset will not succeed here.
  • Excellent judgment under ambiguity, and the operational discipline to run many programs across many markets without dropping quality.

When you join Sysdig, you can expect

  • Extra days off to prioritize your well-being
  • 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan with a 3% company match
  • Maternity and Parental Leave
  • Mental health support for you and your family through the Modern Health app
  • Full health benefits package for you and your family
The U.S. annual salary range for this full-time position is between 170,000 and 213,000 USD/year. Actual offers may be higher or lower than this range based on a variety of factors, including your work location, job-related experience and education.
We would love for you to join us! Please reach out even if your experience doesn't perfectly match the job description. We can always explore other options after starting the conversation. Your background and passion will set you apart, especially if your career path is different.

jobs.excerpt: Our CompanyThe North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) is a not-for-profit international regulatory authority whose mission is to assure the effective and efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid.
jobs.description:
Our Company

The North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) is a not-for-profit international regulatory authority whose mission is to assure the effective and efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid. NERC develops and enforces Reliability Standards; annually assesses seasonal and long‐term reliability; monitors the bulk power system through system awareness; and educates, trains, and certifies industry personnel. NERC’s area of responsibility spans the continental United States, Canada, and the northern portion of Baja California, Mexico. NERC is the Electric Reliability Organization (ERO) for North America, subject to oversight by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and provincial authorities in Canada. NERC’s jurisdiction includes users, owners, and operators of the bulk power system, which serves nearly 400 million people.

Our Mission

The vision for the ERO Enterprise, which is comprised of NERC and the six Regional Entities, is a highly reliable and secure North American bulk power system. Our mission is to assure the effective and efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid.

Your Impact

The Senior Data & AI Engineer designs and builds the data architecture that makes NERC’s data discoverable, trusted, and consumable by analytics and AI—and delivers production AI capabilities on top of it. This is a hands-on engineering role at the center of NERC’s data modernization and AI adoption: the architecture work exists to make AI and advanced analytics possible, and the AI work proves the architecture.

This role turns strategy into working systems. Partnering with both business and technical units, this engineer will implement governed, AI-ready data foundations and productionize AI solutions that advance NERC’s reliability mission—responsibly, securely, and in compliance with regulatory obligations.

Your Role

This role creates and implements NERC’s enterprise data architecture standards and delivers AI capabilities into production. This includes building the semantic and governed data layers that support analytics across the ERO Enterprise, implementing data quality, lineage, and classification controls appropriate to CEII and confidential information, and engineering AI solutions—from retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines to predictive models—on top of that foundation.

This position reports to the Director, Data Architecture & AI. The Director sets architecture direction: AI solution designs are set in partnership with the Principal AI Architect and business units.

Responsibilities

Data Architecture & Engineering (approximately 60%)

  • Design and implement enterprise data models, modeling standards, and the semantic layer that powers certified analytics and reporting.
  • Working with business units, implement the data catalog, lineage, and data classification framework (including CEII and confidential information handling), with automated data quality testing built into pipelines.
  • Build and evolve data pipelines and integration patterns on NERC’s cloud data platform in partnership with Data Engineers and DBAs.
  • Contribute to the API and data-sharing patterns enabling secure, governed exchange with Regional Entities, E-ISAC, FERC, and internal tools.

AI Engineering (approximately 40%)

  • Build and productize AI solutions designed with the Principal AI Architect, including generative AI, RAG pipelines, LLM integrations, predictive analytics and classification algorithms.
  • Implement and operate MLOps/LLMOps practices: deployment environments, evaluation frameworks, monitoring, and cost management.
  • Stand up and maintain AI platform components such as vector stores, orchestration frameworks, and model serving infrastructure.
  • Prototype high-value AI use cases against governed data to validate architecture decisions and accelerate adoption.
  • Implement AI governance guardrails in code and configuration: data eligibility, usage constraints, and model documentation aligned with NIST AI RMF and NERC AI governance.

Shared

  • Ensure solutions comply with regulatory frameworks, internal controls, and NERC requirements.
  • Communicate technical concepts clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, document architectures, standards, and operational runbooks.
  • Evaluate tools and vendors; make build-vs-buy recommendations.

Qualifications

The successful candidate will have at a minimum:

  • 7+ years of firsthand experience in data engineering, data architecture, or ML/AI engineering.
  • Expert-level SQL and Python.
  • Experience with cloud data platforms (Azure, AWS, or GCP) and modern warehouse/Lakehouse architectures; experience with transformation frameworks such as Azure Data Factory or equivalent. Preference is for Microsoft Fabric Dataflow.
  • Practical generative AI experience: RAG, embeddings, vector stores, prompt, and model evaluation—with at least one AI capability shipped to production.
  • Working knowledge of MLOps/LLMOps practices and tooling.
  • Experience with data governance, metadata management, and data quality tooling.
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills, including active listening and clear articulation.
  • Demonstrated ability to work through ambiguity and drive results.

Preferred candidates will also have:

  • Experience in regulated industries, energy, utilities, or reliability organizations.
  • Familiarity with NIST AI RMF, or similar risk/governance frameworks.
  • Experience with platforms such as Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, or Snowflake, and with BI semantic models (e.g., Power BI).
  • Experience with master data management (MDM) and API-based data sharing.

Other

  • A background check will be conducted prior to employment.
  • In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification document form upon hire.
  • This position has been classified as exempt.
  • The position may be based remotely but must be able to travel to NERC offices or meeting locations if needed. Reimbursement of travel expenses will be in accordance with the company’s travel and expense reimbursement policies.
  • Travel is necessary several times a year.

Our Culture Declarations

  • Everyone at NERC is a leader.
  • We are accountable personally and organizationally to deliver on commitments.
  • We develop ourselves and people in the organization to ensure that NERC realizes its strategic objectives.
  • We are resilient and adaptable to the challenges and needs of the business and our team.
  • We exude a growth mindset and empower teams to take risks.
  • We build collaborative relationships within NERC, the ERO, and the stakeholders of NERC.
  • We exemplify NERC cultural behaviors:
    • Reward high-quality, creative, and innovative work.
    • Attract, engage, and retain top talent.
    • Value and respect diverse perspectives
    • Provide a safe, inclusive, and collaborative work environment.
    • Form strong relationships within the company, and with the ERO Enterprise

Who we are

Domino Data Lab powers model-driven businesses with its leading Enterprise AI platform trusted by over 20% of the Fortune 100. What we are building

The Release Engineering & Vulnerability Remediation team is building the infrastructure and automation that lets Domino ship hardened, auditable software to our most security-sensitive customers—federal agencies, financial institutions, and healthcare organizations operating in regulated or air-gapped environments.

Concretely, we are building:

  • A hardened release pipeline that produces container images meeting strict scan thresholds, with reproducible builds and minimal attack surface
  • An automated vulnerability triage system that ingests scanner output, deduplicates findings across images and releases, routes to owners, and tracks SLA compliance—without manual triage
  • Provenance and exploitability tooling that generates SBOMs and VEX statements on every release, so customer security questions are answered from standing artifacts rather than one-off investigations
  • A scalable remediation practice that uses AI and automation to keep pace with the volume of findings, rather than throwing engineers at each CVE individually

This is foundational work. The tooling and runbooks you build will define how Domino operates in regulated markets for years to come.

What your impact will be

In your first year, you will

  • In your first year, you will own the hardened image pipeline for our most demanding deployments and cut time-to-remediate for critical and high findings to a published, defensible SLA.
  • You will replace one-off vulnerability firefighting with an automated path from scan to fix, including SBOM and exploitability statements generated on every release.

  • You will set the technical direction and tooling that the next engineers on this team build on.

  • Experience shipping and maintaining software or container images into regulated, on-premises, or air-gapped environments where you cannot simply redeploy to fix a problem
  • Deep fluency with container build systems, base image strategy, and reproducible builds, plus working knowledge of Kubernetes and Helm packaging

Role Title: Physical Sciences Research Assistant

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote

micro1 is engaging Physical Sciences Research Assistants to contribute specialized expertise to a customer's innovative project. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.

Scope of Work

  1. Design and author advanced evaluation tasks in the physical sciences, encompassing experimental analysis, computational modeling, and technical reasoning.
  2. Source, synthesize, and curate authentic research artifacts, including datasets (CSVs, spreadsheets), computational results, and scientific references.
  3. Craft scenarios and problem statements reflecting the complexity of real-world technical challenges, avoiding simplified or textbook-based examples.
  4. Define rigorous methodological approaches and quantitative solutions for each task.
  5. Develop detailed, 35+ item grading rubrics that assess technical rigor, numerical accuracy, interpretation quality, and adherence to scientific protocols.
  6. Document protocols and experimental reasoning with clarity to ensure reproducibility and rubric fidelity.
  7. Collaborate with project leads to ensure each task meets high standards of methodological integrity and benchmark relevance.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Bachelor's or Master's degree in physics, chemistry, materials science, or a closely related discipline.
  2. Minimum of 2 years of hands-on research experience or applied technical project work in a physical sciences domain.
  3. Proven methodological rigor and strong quantitative analysis skills in scientific contexts.
  4. Demonstrated ability to document complex technical procedures and results in clear, professional written English.
  5. Experience authoring or evaluating scientific rubrics or assessments is a plus.
  6. Familiarity with handling large volumes of technical data and diverse document formats (e.g., PDFs, spreadsheets).
  7. Commitment to high standards of protocol and rubric fidelity throughout project assignments.

Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete work may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow. Minimum submission requirements apply. Experts must submit a minimum of tasks per week.

Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts ready to jump in right away. If selected, we expect you to start your first tasks within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

BI Developer – MHPI

The BI Developer builds and operates the enterprise dashboards, semantic models, and reporting assets that make

Dashboard & Report Development

normalization, and reporting.

solutions.

Technical Skills

• Strong understanding of the medallion architecture (bronze / silver / gold) and how BI consumes governed
enterprise data.

large volumes of data.

This role is intended to add recruiting capacity for a period of approximately 6 months (September 2026 – February 2027) with an anticipated workload of 20–40 hours per week; volume will vary with interview activity and open requisition load.

Since our founding in 1994, Prosci has been laser-focused on change. By combining our deep understanding of people with a proven methodology rooted in the creation of the ADKAR® model, we’ve helped countless people and organizations thrive. Our solutions empower customers with lasting change resiliency through a unique blend of training, advisory services, and licensing options, including Kaiya, our AI change management coach.

At Prosci, we are a purpose-driven organization full of passionate, curious, and results-oriented people. Working at Prosci means being part of a dynamic team that is dedicated to our purpose of creating a world where change is done right. Join us and be part of a culture that thrives on continuous learning, growth, and making a difference.

Check out our website for more about our team and approach: .

Key Responsibilities

Recruiting

  • Manage full life cycle recruiting for assigned US and Canadian requisitions: intake, sourcing, screening, interview coordination, assessment administration, reference and background checks, and offer support.
  • Lead intake and needs analysis conversations with hiring managers to confirm role scope, must-have criteria, and hiring timeline before opening a requisition.
  • Partner with HRBPs to create and publish job descriptions and postings.
  • Source active and passive candidates using Prosci's ATS (Workable), LinkedIn Recruiter, job boards, employee referrals, and other channels.
  • Conduct phone screens, coordinate interview loops, administer assessments, and lead scorecard completion and debrief discussions with interview teams.
  • Maintain regular, high-quality communication with candidates throughout the process to protect the candidate’s experience.
  • Support offer construction and, in partnership with the hiring HRBP and hiring manager, help negotiate terms with candidates.

Pipeline, Compliance, and Candidate Experience

  • Build and maintain candidate pipelines for roles that recur or are historically difficult to fill.
  • Apply sourcing, screening, and interview practices consistent with Prosci's commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion, including attention to underexplored talent pools.
  • Apply working knowledge of US and Canadian hiring requirements relevant to recruiting (for example, pay transparency rules, background check requirements, and state or provincial variation) and flag questions to HR Business Partners rather than making independent compliance calls.
  • Perform select preboarding activities for new hires from the point of offer acceptance to start date, including internal stakeholder communication, coordination of first day logistics, and scheduling of week 1 core onboarding sessions.

Reporting and Process

  • Keep candidate and requisition records current and accurate in the ATS (Workable).
  • Provide regular pipeline and hiring status updates to hiring managers and HR Business Partners.
  • Flag process friction or candidate experience issues to HR Business Partners and suggest improvements.

Requirements

Required Skills and Experience

  • Full life cycle recruiting experience across sourcing, screening, interviewing, and offer support, ideally spanning both US and Canadian hiring. Working knowledge of US and Canadian employment and hiring practices, with good judgment about when to escalate a compliance question (only US is required).
  • Working proficiency with an applicant tracking system and with LinkedIn Recruiter or an equivalent sourcing tool.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, comfortable managing multiple candidates, requisitions, and hiring manager relationships at once.
  • Ability to work independently against a defined requisition load with minimal day-to-day oversight.
  • Comfort using AI tools across the recruiting life cycle, primarily to synthesize interview notes and scorecard feedback into clear, evidence-based debrief summaries and candidate recommendations, with sound judgment about reviewing AI output for accuracy and bias before it informs a hiring decision.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of in-house or agency recruiting experience.
  • Demonstrated experience recruiting across a range of levels, from individual contributor through professional or exempt roles.
  • Experience recruiting for professional services, consulting, or other high-growth organization is a plus.
  • Prior contract or interim recruiting experience, comfortable ramping quickly on a new team's process and requisitions.
  • Experience with Predictive Index or a similar behavioral assessment tool.
  • Familiarity with competency-based, inclusive interviewing practices.

Additional Information

Work Location: Remote within the US or Canada.

Compensation: Up to $65.00/hr.

Travel Requirements: None,

Position Description

Associate Director, State Policy

Department:Policy & Strategy
Reports To:Director of Policy
FLSA Status:Exempt
Employment Type:Full time
Location:Remote, travel up to 15%

About Community Catalyst

Community Catalyst is the national health justice organization working to ensure care is accessible, affordable, and accountable to the people it serves—and that racial bias does not determine who receives care. For more than two decades, Community Catalyst has partnered with state and community advocates to change systems before harm occurs. The organization integrates policy reform, community organizing, data science, narrative strategy, and thought leadership to advance structural change in health care.

The Opportunity

The Associate Director for State Policy is responsible for assisting the Director of Policy and Vice President for Policy & Government Affairs in developing and carrying out Community Catalyst’s state policy agenda, ensuring alignment with federal policy priorities and partner needs.

The individual in this position will provide leadership to the policy team in identifying and capitalizing on trends in state health policy and help shape the support that Community Catalyst provides to partners across our programs and projects. The individual will need to work with colleagues across the organization, think about how various initiatives intersect, and how we coordinate and collaborate within the organization.

The individual is expected to motivate policy team colleagues and technical assistance providers to consistently provide excellent service to our external partners as well as represent the needs and goals of those partners within the organization. The individual will also need to build relationships with external partners – including state and community based organizations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Partners with the Director of Policy, Vice President for Policy & Government Affairs, and senior management team in development of Community Catalyst’s state policy agenda, including efforts that are centered in community leadership.
  • Conducts and coordinates analysis of state and federal legislative and regulatory proposals and monitors state policy trends and progress.
  • Coordinates processes to ensure that state voices are represented in the development of federal policy priorities.
  • With the Programs team, develops and coordinates program and issue-specific policy goals, technical assistance strategies, and evaluate progress over time.
  • Develops and maintains expertise in key health policy areas and serves as an advisor and thought leader on key policy issues at the state and federal level.
  • Supports the organization’s efforts to strengthen local community organization engagement around health issues and build collaborative partnerships with state policy advocates around a jointly developed agenda.
  • With the Communications team, writes issue briefs, blogs and other materials to help educate policy makers, advocates and other audiences.
  • Builds and maintains strategic relationships and represents the organization with policymakers, funders and state, national and community-based organizations.
  • Plays a supporting role in fundraising, including strategy, funder/donor outreach and stewardship, proposal writing and reporting.
  • Performs other duties as necessary to achieve the goals of the policy team and the organization.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree plus at least 8 years relevant work experience in health policy or a combination of relevant higher education and years of legal and/or health policy work experience.
  • Demonstrated in-depth knowledge of health policy issues, ability to analyze complex and intersecting health legislation, regulations and policies, and understanding the connections between state political environments and effects on advocacy and policy campaigns.
  • Understanding of the state and federal policy landscape and trends and the policymaking process.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to travel on average 3-5 times a year.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Masters degree in public policy, public health, public administration or related field.
  • Demonstrated experience leading or supporting state-level policy campaigns.
  • Extensive knowledge of state Medicaid, Marketplace, and related programs and policies.
  • Experience engaging with state policymakers, legislators, and public program officials.

Core Competencies

  • Ability to oversee multiple tasks with high attention to detail.
  • Commitment to health equity, racial justice and experience in social change activism.
  • Exceptional organization, policy analysis, written and oral communication skills.
  • Proven skills in relationship development.
  • Versatile team player with strong collaboration, conflict management and management skills.
  • Ability to work independently and manage one’s own time.

Supervisory Responsibilities

The Associate Director for State Policy may supervise junior policy staff such as Policy Associates, Policy Analysts, or seasonal interns.

Work Environment & Physical Requirements

This is a remote, office-based position performed from a home or remote workspace using standard office equipment and technology. Occasional travel may be required based on organizational needs. The role involves extended periods of sitting, regular computer use, and virtual communication. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the role.

Compensation & Benefits

The salary range for this position is $100,000– $120,000 based on a full-time schedule. Placement within the range is determined by role scope, relevant experience, skills, geographic considerations, and internal equity. Compensation is reviewed and approved in accordance with Community Catalyst’s compensation framework and organizational policies.

This position is eligible for Community Catalyst’s employee benefits program, subject to plan terms and eligibility requirements. Benefits may include medical, dental, and vision coverage; life and disability insurance; flexible spending accounts; retirement savings; paid time off and holidays; paid family and medical leave; wellness benefits; and other programs as outlined in the Employee Benefits Guide. Benefit offerings and eligibility may vary based on employment status, role classification, location, and collective bargaining agreements, where applicable. Benefits are governed by plan documents and may be modified from time to time.

Employment Opportunity Statement

Community Catalyst is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing a workplace free from discrimination and harassment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Disclaimer

This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of duties. Responsibilities may change based on organizational needs, and reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

jobs.excerpt: Role Overview 1Kosmos is seeking a Senior Director of Healthcare Sales to lead and accelerate commercial growth across the healthcare vertical.
jobs.description:
Role Overview

1Kosmos is seeking a Senior Director of Healthcare Sales to lead and accelerate commercial growth across the healthcare vertical. This is a senior individual contributor and market development role for someone who understands how digital identity, authentication, and regulatory compliance intersect in hospital systems, pharmaceutical companies, and health insurance payers, and who can convert that understanding into closed enterprise revenue.

1Kosmos has built significant momentum in healthcare, with deployments spanning identity verification for patient onboarding, account recovery, and step-up authentication; enterprise and shared workstation passwordless authentication for clinical and administrative staff; and Electronic Prescribing of Controlled Substances (EPCS) workflows that meet DEA logical access control requirements. The platform is certified to NIST 800-63-3 at Identity Assurance Level 2 (IAL2), holds a FedRAMP High authorization, achieves Department of Defense Impact Level 4 (IL4), and is Kantara-certified as a full Credential Service Provider (CSP), one of fewer than a dozen vendors globally at that level.

This role will own the healthcare go-to-market strategy and execution, drive pipeline from initial engagement through close, and work cross-functionally with Solutions Engineering, Product, Marketing, and Customer Success to deliver outcomes for health system, pharma, and payer customers.

Key Responsibilities

Market Development and Pipeline Generation

  • Build and own the healthcare vertical sales strategy, targeting hospital systems and integrated delivery networks (IDNs), pharmaceutical manufacturers and distributors, and health insurance payers.
  • Generate pipeline through direct outreach, partner co-sell motions, industry events (Health-ISAC, HIMSS, ViVE, HLTH), and referral networks across CISO, CMIO, CISO, and IT leadership audiences.
  • Develop and maintain a qualified pipeline sufficient to support consistent quarterly and annual revenue targets.
  • Identify and pursue whitespace opportunities across the 1Kosmos healthcare use case portfolio, including patient identity, workforce identity, EPCS, and clinical shared workstation authentication.

Sales Execution and Deal Management

  • Own the full sales cycle from discovery through contract execution on net-new and expansion opportunities.
  • Lead executive-level engagement with CISO, CIO, CMIO, VP of Identity, and Procurement stakeholders.
  • Articulate 1Kosmos' differentiated value across ID verification (onboarding, account recovery, step-up), enterprise and shared workstation passwordless authentication, and EPCS use cases.
  • Navigate complex, multi-stakeholder deal cycles including security reviews, legal, procurement, and compliance approvals common to health system purchasing environments.
  • Work with channel partners including Optiv, VARs, and GSIs on partner-assisted and partner-sourced deals.

Customer and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Act as the primary executive sponsor and relationship owner for strategic healthcare accounts throughout the sales cycle.
  • Engage clinical and operational leaders to translate identity security requirements into business outcomes, including reduced help desk volume, HIPAA compliance support, DEA EPCS compliance, and reduced risk of credential-based breaches.
  • Partner with Solutions Engineering on proof-of-concept design and execution, ensuring technical validation aligns with customer requirements.
  • Coordinate with Customer Success post-sale to support smooth onboarding and expansion planning.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with the SVP of Sales on territory planning, forecast accuracy, and executive account strategy.
  • Partner with Marketing on healthcare-specific campaigns, event strategy, and collateral including case studies, use case briefs, and competitive positioning.
  • Provide structured feedback to Product on healthcare-specific requirements including Epic integration depth, EPCS workflow needs, and regulatory certification gaps.
  • Collaborate with the Partnerships team to activate and co-sell with systems integrators and technology alliance partners active in healthcare.

Reporting and Forecast Management

  • Maintain accurate pipeline, opportunity, and forecast data in CRM.
  • Provide regular updates to the SVP of Sales on progress, risks, blockers, and competitive intelligence.
  • Track and report on key performance metrics including pipeline coverage, win rates, average contract value, and time to close.

The 1Kosmos Healthcare Opportunity

Healthcare is one of the most active verticals for identity security investment. Credential-based breaches account for a large share of healthcare data incidents. HIPAA Security Rule requirements, DEA EPCS regulations, and the administrative burden of shared workstation environments in clinical settings create specific, high-urgency demand for what 1Kosmos provides.

1Kosmos is the only platform that combines IAL2-certified identity verification with enterprise-grade passwordless authentication in a single architecture that sits on top of existing identity infrastructure. The platform integrates natively with Epic MyChart for patient identity workflows, Microsoft Entra Verified ID for verifiable credential issuance, Okta and Ping for enterprise SSO environments, ServiceNow for ITSM-integrated identity events, Workday for workforce onboarding, and identity governance platforms including SailPoint and Saviynt. Additional integrations span CyberArk, Broadcom, and multiple applicant tracking systems (ATS) for pre-hire identity verification.

Certifications relevant to healthcare customers include:

  • NIST 800-63-3 at IAL2, supporting identity assurance requirements for clinical and administrative access
  • FedRAMP High authorization, relevant for health systems and payers serving federal programs including Medicare and Medicaid
  • DoD Impact Level 4 (IL4), establishing the platform's suitability for sensitive health data environments
  • Kantara full CSP certification, one of fewer than a dozen globally, supporting highest-assurance identity proofing workflows
  • iBeta PAD Level 2 for liveness detection, directly relevant to anti-spoofing requirements in EPCS logical access control
  • SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, and GDPR compliance

What Success Looks Like

  • A qualified pipeline of healthcare opportunities across hospital systems, pharma, and payers is built and maintained with strong coverage ratios.
  • Net-new enterprise logos are closed on a consistent quarterly cadence.
  • 1Kosmos is recognized as a credible, differentiated vendor in healthcare identity and EPCS workflows.
  • Relationships with key health system CISO, CIO, and CMIO stakeholders are established and active.
  • Healthcare-specific use case narratives, case studies, and reference customers are developed in partnership with Marketing.

Requirements

Qualifications

  • 10 or more years of enterprise software sales experience, with at least five years focused on the healthcare vertical (hospital systems, health systems, IDNs, pharma, or payers).
  • Demonstrated track record of closing six- and seven-figure SaaS or software deals with health system buyers.
  • Deep familiarity with the healthcare purchasing environment including CISO, CIO, CMIO, Procurement, and Legal stakeholders, and typical 6- to 18-month enterprise deal cycles.
  • Working knowledge of relevant regulatory and compliance frameworks including HIPAA, DEA EPCS requirements, and NIST identity standards.
  • Experience selling into or around electronic health record (EHR) environments, particularly Epic, is strongly preferred.
  • Comfort operating in a high-growth, fast-moving environment with evolving processes and significant individual ownership.
  • Excellent communication and executive presence; able to operate credibly at the C-suite level with both clinical and IT audiences.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with identity, access management, digital identity, or cybersecurity platforms.
  • Prior sales experience at or against vendors such as Imprivata, Ping Identity, Okta, Microsoft, or CyberArk in a healthcare context.
  • Existing relationships with health system CISO, CIO, or VP of Identity leaders.
  • Familiarity with EPCS logical access control requirements and the DEA IFR/Final Rule framework.
  • Background in channel or partner-assisted selling through resellers, systems integrators, or GSIs.

Why 1Kosmos

1Kosmos is the trust platform for identity, operating at the intersection of identity verification, passwordless authentication, and verified credential reuse. Processing more than 2 billion authentications per year at five-nines availability, and recognized as a leader in passwordless authentication for the enterprise by KuppingerCole, 1Kosmos is at an inflection point of scale and market category definition.

Healthcare represents one of the clearest problem-to-solution fits in the market. The combination of regulatory pressure, credential-based breach risk, and high-friction clinical identity workflows creates a compelling, high-urgency buying environment. This role joins a company with proven deployments, differentiated certifications, and the platform integrations required to win in this space.

Benefits

  • Remote / flexible work model
  • Medical / Dental / Vision
  • 401(k)
  • Unlimited PTO

Principal Software Engineer, (Libraries Platform)

The role:

At Chainguard, we think the best platform work is invisible: the libraries just appear, the builds just work, and the CVEs quietly regret their life choices.

Chainguard's Libraries organization runs the secure, reliable factory that continuously builds, verifies, and serves open-source libraries to customers and internal teams across multiple ecosystems. We're expanding that factory to new inbound ecosystems, while raising the bar on how much of the remediation and build lifecycle runs without a human in the loop.

As a Principal Software Engineer on the Libraries Platform team, you'll set technical direction for that expansion. This is a strategic, cross-organizational platform role: you're not just operating the existing factory, you're deciding how it generalizes to ecosystems it wasn't originally built for, and how much of the remediation pipeline - from CVE detection through patch, rebuild, verification, and release - can become fully automated rather than engineer-mediated. Your decisions will shape the platform's architecture for years and influence how every ecosystem team builds on top of it.

What you’ll do:

  • Own the technical strategy for multi-ecosystem scaling. Define the architecture that lets the Libraries Platform onboard new language ecosystems (.NET, Go, Rust) without re-deriving core services per ecosystem: generalizing package indexing, build orchestration, and metadata services so they're ecosystem-agnostic where possible and cleanly extensible where not.

  • Drive end-to-end remediation automation. Lead the redesign of CVE remediation workflows to close the loop from detection to verified, released fix with minimal manual intervention, rebuild triggering, SBOM and provenance regeneration, policy verification, and rollout, across all supported ecosystems.

  • Push the frontier on novel patch generation. Set the direction for agentic/AI-driven systems that synthesize security fixes when no upstream patch exists yet — not just selecting or backporting existing ones — and design the guardrails (automated validation, regression testing, provenance, and human checkpoints) that make machine-generated patches safe to ship across ecosystems.

  • Set platform-wide technical direction, spanning the package index, build/packaging pipelines, registry mirrors, and orchestration tooling that serve external customers and internal ecosystem teams at scale.

  • Make foundational build vs. buy and sequencing calls for bringing .NET, Go, and Rust online, identifying what's genuinely novel about each ecosystem's toolchain, packaging, and dependency model, and what can reuse or extend existing platform primitives.

  • Partner at the org level with Ecosystem teams (Java, JavaScript, Python/AI/ML, and new-language leads), Platform, Delivery, Sustaining, and Security to align the platform roadmap with where the business is taking on new ecosystem risk and commitments.

  • Raise the technical bar across the org: mentor Staff and Senior Engineers, drive design reviews for the biggest architectural bets, and write the docs and RFCs that let other teams build correctly on the platform without you in the room.

  • Own reliability and scalability at the platform level: define SLOs for the expanded remediation pipeline, and lead incident response and postmortems for the platform's most consequential failures.

  • Get hands-on when it matters: dig into toolchain, compiler, and dependency-resolution problems specific to new ecosystems (e.g., NuGet, Go modules, Cargo) when they threaten the pipeline's reliability or timeline.

What we’re looking for:

  • 12+ years designing, building, and operating infrastructure for language ecosystems or developer platforms, (build systems, package registries, or CI/CD serving widely-used libraries or services) with demonstrated Principal-level scope: setting technical direction across multiple teams, not just owning a single system.

  • Direct experience standing up or significantly extending platform support for a language ecosystem- i.e. you've done the "onboard a new toolchain/packaging model into an existing platform" problem before, ideally including .NET (NuGet), Go (modules), or Rust (Cargo).

  • Strong proficiency in Go, with the judgment to know when a new ecosystem's idioms should bend the platform and when the platform should hold its ground.

  • A track record of automating away manual remediation steps. You can point to a workflow you took from "engineer does this by hand" to "system does this reliably," including the judgment calls about where automation is safe and where a human checkpoint still matters.

  • Deep background in CI/CD, agentic pipelines, cloud-native infrastructure, and IaC: containers (Docker/OCI, Kubernetes), Terraform, and pipeline tooling (GitHub Actions, Argo, Tekton, or equivalents) with experience running these at scale across heterogeneous ecosystems.

  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose and resolve deep toolchain, compiler, and packaging failures across multiple ecosystems, and to turn one-off fixes into systemic prevention.

  • Excellent written communication in a remote, distributed environment. Principal-level influence here happens mostly through docs, RFCs, and review, not just code.

  • A Principal ownership mindset: you set direction other engineers build against, you're comfortable being the person who has to make the ecosystem-generalization call with incomplete information, and you actively shape both the roadmap and engineering culture. Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based, not permanent employment.

What this opportunity involves We're building a dataset to evaluate AI coding agents - how well a model handles real-world developer tasks.

You'll create challenging tasks and evaluation criteria within realistic simulated environments:

  • Build realistic developer environments - a virtual company with codebase, infrastructure, and context (tickets, docs, conversations) that forms a believable development history
  • Design tasks from intermediate states of these environments - craft the prompt, define what "solved" means, and ensure the task is solvable by an AI agent
  • Write tests that verify agent solutions - accept all valid approaches and reject incorrect ones, neither too strict nor too lenient
  • Iterate on tasks and tests based on QA feedback - review agent solutions, analyze failures, and refine until the evaluation is fair and robust

What this is NOT

  • Not data labeling
  • Not prompt engineering
  • Not writing code from scratch - the agent writes most of the code; you guide and evaluate

  • Core stack: Python (FastAPI), JavaScript/TypeScript (React), Docker, Postgres, Kafka, Redis
  • Experience writing tests (functional, integration)

Why this is hard

Frontier models are already good at coding. Creating a task that genuinely challenges the best models is non-trivial. You need to deeply understand where models fail and what scenarios reveal the difference between a good and a bad solution. Tasks have many valid solutions - writing tests that accept all correct solutions and reject incorrect ones is harder than it sounds.

How it works

Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join a project → Complete tasks → Get paid
